corrected_content.problem: Consider the function $g(x, y) = \frac{x^{2}}{y}$. What is the rate of change of $g(x, y)$ at the point $(2, 1)$ in the direction of the vector $\mathbf{v}=⟨-1,3⟩$?
corrected_content.worked_solution:
The gradient is $
abla g=\langle2x/y,-x^2/y^2angle$, so $
abla g(2,1)=\langle4,-4angle$. Normalize the direction: $u=\langle-1,3angle/\sqrt{10}$. Hence $$D_ug=
abla g\cdot u= rac{-4-12}{\sqrt{10}}=- rac{8\sqrt{10}}5.$$
